options.why: Divided $7$ by $63$, putting the quantities the wrong way around.
Subtracted the two quantities instead of dividing.

options.why: Divided by $3$ instead of $3.5$, ignoring the decimal part of the mass.
Divided $3.5$ by $21$, inverting the rate.
Multiplied $21$ by $3.5$ instead of dividing.

questions.question_text:
A job pays $\$95$ for $6$ hours.
Give the unit rate in $\$$/h, correct to the nearest cent.

options.why: Rounded $15.8333\ldots$ up, but the third decimal is $3$, so it rounds down.
Rounded to the nearest dollar instead of the nearest cent.
Cut the division off at one decimal place and wrote a zero for the cents.

questions.question_text:
A tank holding $4500$ L empties completely in $15$ minutes.
Express this as a unit rate.

options.why: The number is right, but the time was given in minutes, so the rate is per minute, not per second.
Subtracted the time from the capacity instead of dividing.
Multiplied the capacity by the time instead of dividing.

questions.question_text:
A car travels $180$ km on $15$ L of petrol.
Express this as a rate in L/km, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Divided the distance by the capacity, which gives km/L, not L/km.
Subtracted the capacity from the distance instead of dividing.
Multiplied the two quantities instead of dividing.

questions.solution_text:
L/km means litres on top and kilometres underneath.
$\frac{15\text{ L}}{180\text{ km}}$
$=\frac{0.0833\ldots\text{ L}}{1\text{ km}}$
$=0.08\text{ L/km}$

questions.question_text:
A seedling was $24$ cm tall on day $1$ and $66$ cm tall on day $8$.
Find its average rate of growth per day.

options.why: Divided the growth of $42$ cm by $8$ instead of by the $7$ days between the two readings.
Divided the final height $66$ by the day number $8$ instead of using the changes.
Gave the total growth without dividing by the number of days.

questions.solution_text:
$66-24=42$ cm of growth
$8-1=7$ days
$\frac{42\text{ cm}}{7\text{ days}}$
$=\frac{6\text{ cm}}{1\text{ day}}$
$=6\text{ cm/day}$

questions.question_text:
A car park held $320$ cars at $9$ am and $500$ cars at noon.
Find the average rate of increase in cars per hour.

options.why: Divided the increase of $180$ cars by $4$ hours instead of the $3$ hours from $9$ am to noon.
Divided the final count $500$ by the clock time $9$ instead of using the changes.
Gave the total increase in cars without dividing by the time.

questions.solution_text:
$500-320=180$ more cars
$9$ am to noon is $3$ hours.
$\frac{180\text{ cars}}{3\text{ h}}$
$=\frac{60\text{ cars}}{1\text{ h}}$
$=60\text{ cars/h}$
